prompt: It is January 2, 2019. I would like to outperform the S&P 500 over the next five years. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy? Answer as of that date.
reply:
# 10 Stocks to Buy on January 2, 2019

**A caveat first:** I know how 2019–2023 turned out, so I can't make a truly blind pick. Any list I build now carries hindsight bias, even if every reason given uses only information available then. I've limited the reasoning to 2019-era facts and shown the actual results at the end so you can judge for yourself.

## Market backdrop (January 2019)
- The S&P 500 just fell almost 20% from its September peak. The causes were a December Fed rate hike, the US-China trade war and fears of slowing growth.
- Quality growth stocks were sold off hard with everything else, so strong franchises were trading at more reasonable prices.
- **Strategy:** buy durable, cash-generating businesses with long growth runways while they're discounted, and hold for five years.

## The list

| # | Company | Ticker | Thesis as of Jan 2019 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Microsoft | MSFT | Azure is growing about 75% a year, and Office is shifting to subscriptions. It's becoming a recurring-revenue cloud company. |
| 2 | Amazon | AMZN | AWS is growing about 45% and is highly profitable. Advertising is an emerging second profit engine. The stock is down about 35% from its highs. |
| 3 | Alphabet | GOOGL | It dominates search, owns YouTube, has a growing cloud unit and holds over $100B in net cash. |
| 4 | Facebook | FB | At about $131 it trades near 17x earnings despite 30%+ revenue growth. The Cambridge Analytica fallout looks priced in. |
| 5 | Visa | V | It collects a "toll" on the global shift from cash to digital payments, with very high margins and a light balance sheet. |
| 6 | UnitedHealth | UNH | It's the largest US insurer, and Optum (data, pharmacy benefits, care delivery) is a fast-growing second business. |
| 7 | Nvidia | NVDA | The stock is down about 55% from its October high because of a crypto-driven inventory glut. That looks temporary, while its data-center and AI-training GPUs are a long-term growth market. |
| 8 | Taiwan Semiconductor | TSM | It's the leading-edge chip foundry and ahead at 7nm while Intel struggles at 10nm. It trades at a modest valuation and pays a dividend. |
| 9 | Adobe | ADBE | Its subscription transition is complete, it effectively owns creative software, and it's expanding into digital marketing. |
| 10 | Costco | COST | Its membership-fee model makes it resilient in a recession, with high renewal rates and steady store growth. |

**Construction notes:**
- Equal-weight the ten names and rebalance once a year.
- The portfolio leans heavily toward tech and growth, so it will swing more than the index.
- A more cautious investor might hold this as a satellite around an S&P 500 index core.

## Reality check: what actually happened
These are approximate split-adjusted price changes from the end of 2018 to the end of 2023, excluding dividends.

| Stock | Approx. change |
|---|---|
| NVDA | ~+1,380% |
| MSFT | ~+270% |
| COST | ~+225% |
| TSM | ~+180% |
| META (FB) | ~+170% |
| GOOGL | ~+165% |
| ADBE | ~+165% |
| UNH | ~+110% |
| AMZN | ~+100% |
| V | ~+97% |
| **Equal-weight portfolio** | **~+285%** (~+165% without NVDA) |
| **S&P 500** | **~+90% price / ~+107% total return** |

The list beats the index by a wide margin, and **that's exactly why you should be skeptical of it.** Knowing the outcomes shaped which names came to mind. Nvidia alone drives much of the gap, and a genuine January 2019 analyst could just as easily have picked PayPal (roughly −27%), Disney (down), Intel (flat) or Netflix (lagged the index), each with an equally convincing story at the time.

If you're using this to test a strategy or a forecasting process, I can instead build a rules-based list, such as quality and valuation screens using only data available in 2019, which would be a fairer out-of-sample test.
